cohort: The study included 900 women hospitalized after 28 weeks of gestation who met inclusion criteria, undergoing either primary or repeat caesarean sections.
finding: If managed appropriately, repeat caesarean section may result in vaginal delivery despite increased maternal risks, and elective repeat CS at 39 weeks may avoid preterm birth.
mod_finding: Repeat caesarean sections are associated with increased maternal risks like adhesions and UV fold obliteration, but appropriate management may still lead to successful vaginal delivery.
gest_age: Women hospitalized after 28 weeks of gestation were included; elective repeat CS was recommended at 39 weeks.
